target_customer: Non-developers such as creators, kids and small businesses who wanted to publish Alexa skills; later voice UX designers
problem: Building an Alexa skill required coding and backend setup, which blocked non-developers.
business_model: Freemium SaaS with premium features such as flash briefing scheduling

founders.name: Vasili Shynkarenka
previous_startups: Software agency building chatbots and voice apps (with Abramchuk)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2018-02-02 says both founders are from Belarus and ran an agency for chatbots and voice apps.

founders.name: Maksim Abramchuk
previous_startups: Software agency building chatbots and voice apps (with Shynkarenka)

exit.reason: Storyline ended its no-code builder in late 2018 and renamed itself Invocable; Invocable announced its shutdown on 2019-04-15 and moved users to Voiceflow.

competitors.name: Sayspring
competitors.what: No-code voice app design tool for designers, as a prototyping step
competitors.funding_then: $1.5M raise in May 2017 per a TechCrunch headline linked in the article

competitors.name: Amazon Alexa Skill Blueprints
competitors.what: Amazon template tool to publish personal Alexa skills without code
competitors.traction_then: Announced in April 2018, a few months after the W18 batch

technical_complexity.rationale: A visual builder on top of Amazon's published skill APIs, within reach of two developers with agency experience.

defensibility.rationale: Fully dependent on Amazon's platform, with Amazon itself shipping Blueprints and other builders like Storyflow offering the same.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amazon launched Skill Blueprints in April 2018 and the builder was discontinued in November 2018.

market_need_then: Alexa skills were growing fast in 2018 and Storyline reported 12,000 users who had launched over 2,500 skills by July 2018, mostly hobbyists and kids.

branding.domain_note: getstoryline.com was redirected to Invocable.com at the rename in late 2018, per VoiceBot.

identity.voice_and_tone: Helpful blog tone, with tutorials for skill builders on a Medium blog.

rebrands.why: Company said it needed an identity that fit voice design and chose a name meaning capable of being invoked, avoiding names like apps or flow.

branding.community_and_virality: Often confused with Storyflow, which also built Alexa skills without code and later became Voiceflow, absorbing Storyline users.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name that was confused with a direct rival; the rename to Invocable came with the pivot and did not save the company.

pivots.from: No-code Alexa skill builder with publishing
pivots.to: Invocable, a paid voice UX prototyping tool
pivots.why: Company chose to focus on voice designers after the builder was discontinued

outcome_analysis: Storyline grew quickly on Alexa, raised $770K led by Boost VC in July 2018, then discontinued its builder in November 2018 and became Invocable, a paid tool for voice designers. Amazon had shipped Skill Blueprints in April 2018, and Voiceflow took the no-code users. The pivot lasted about five months before the shutdown in April 2019, so platform dependence, an incumbent move and a failed pivot explain the end.
notes: The $770K round and Boost VC lead come from TechCrunch and VoiceBot, with Crunchbase data cited by VoiceBot saying $770K over two rounds including YC. The Storyflow seed of $500K led by Ripple Ventures is a different company. The website listed in the directory is a Product Hunt page, so the company site is dead and redirected to Invocable.com. The VoiceBot pages were not fetched past a redirect, so shutdown details come from search result summaries.
